subject: science
passage: Scattered across the fields of New England and northern Europe are boulders that seem strangely out of place, their minerals matching no bedrock for many kilometers around. Geologists call them glacial erratics. During the last ice age, advancing sheets of ice tore such rocks from distant outcrops and dragged them slowly across the landscape. When the ice finally melted, it left the boulders stranded on ground of an entirely different ______ surfaces often still scored with long parallel scratches from the journey.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: "When the ice finally melted, it left the boulders stranded on ground of an entirely different type" is a complete sentence. "Their surfaces often still scored with long parallel scratches" has no main verb ("scored" is a participle), so it is an absolute phrase, like "their minerals matching no bedrock" in the first sentence. An absolute phrase is attached to the clause it describes with a comma.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Without a comma, the absolute phrase runs into "type," and "type their surfaces" makes no sense.
explanation.B: Correct. The comma attaches the absolute phrase "their surfaces often still scored …" to the independent clause it describes.
explanation.C: Incorrect. A semicolon must be followed by an independent clause, but "their surfaces often still scored …" has no main verb.
explanation.D: Incorrect. A period would leave "Their surfaces often still scored …" as a sentence fragment.
